candidates.exact_span: EPA proposes a revision to the facility temporary 30-day average TDS net incremental increase limit of 497 mg/L to 449 mg/L.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the operative enforceable TDS limit for FY2025 is the existing 497 mg/L temporary limit or the proposed 449 mg/L revision changes which numeric threshold is used for compliance comparison and exceedance determination.

candidates.exact_span: The proposed TDS permit limit, in accordance with 40 CFR §133.101(f), was based 95th percentile of the most recent three years (i.e., 2018-2020) of City's wastewater treatment plant effluent net TDS data.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether this limit is a net incremental increase concentration limit derived under §133.101(f), and whether the cited 2018–2020 basis governs applicability, affects which TDS metric and limit value are enforceable for reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: The 30-day average mass loading limit is, also, revised to 24,992lbs/day from 27,664 lbs/day based on the proposed 30-day average TDS net incremental increase limit of 449 mg/L.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A different reading of whether the mass loading limit (24,992 lbs/day vs 27,664 lbs/day) is operative, and whether it is tied to the proposed 449 mg/L TDS limit, changes which loading-based numeric limit applies to effluent measurements.

candidates.exact_span: if a discharge poses the reasonable potential to cause an in-stream excursion above a water quality criterion, the permit must contain an effluent limit for that pollutant.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether reasonable-potential findings trigger enforceable effluent limits for specific pollutants affects whether numeric compliance comparisons are applicable versus report-only monitoring for those parameters.

candidates.exact_span: The result of the preliminary RP analysis (see Appendix 2) indicates that Cyanide has RP to violate WQS consistent with the designated uses for the receiving waterbody.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether cyanide is treated as having reasonable potential to violate water quality standards determines whether enforceable cyanide effluent limits must be applied rather than treated as monitoring without a numeric compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: The draft permit will propose a daily maximum and monthly average limits of 22 ug/L and 14.67 ug/L,
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether these proposed cyanide limits (daily maximum 22 ug/L and monthly average 14.67 ug/L) are operative for FY2025, and which averaging period applies to each reported measurement, changes exceedance evaluation and limit applicability.

candidates.exact_span: The facility is required to continue maintaining the formulated BMP activities and monitoring its effluent quality and quantity on a regular basis with reporting results monthly.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether ongoing BMP maintenance, effluent quality/quantity monitoring, and monthly reporting are binding permit obligations affects which monitoring requirements were applicable in FY2025 (B) and how to classify months or parameters lacking reported results—e.g., required monitoring without adequate evidence versus other documented no-data states (C).

candidates.exact_span: The facility is designated a major POTW for permitting purposes and must supply the expanded pollutant testing list described in the EPA Application Form 2A.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Classification as a major POTW and the obligation to supply the Form 2A expanded pollutant testing list affects which monitoring requirements are applicable for the facility during the evaluated period.

candidates.exact_span: They completed Part D, "Expanded Effluent Testing Data" of form 2A and submitted to EPA as a part of their April 13, 2021 application.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether Part D expanded effluent testing obligations from the 2021 application carry forward as ongoing monitoring requirements affects which parameters required monitoring in FY2025 (B) and whether absence of results for those parameters reflects unmet obligations or another documented state (C).
